title: SQL query built by concatenating user-controlled input
message: customerID flows from POST /v1/orders → FindByCustomer without parameterization.
why: Anyone who controls customerID can append arbitrary SQL — reading other customers' orders or altering data. This path is reachable from the public guest-checkout API without authentication.
fix: Pass values as query parameters so the driver escapes them. Build optional clauses with placeholders instead of string concatenation.

title: Live Stripe secret key hard-coded in configuration class
message: Matches Stripe live secret key pattern sk_live_… (entropy 4.9 bits/char).
why: The key grants full access to the Stripe account — charges, refunds and customer data. It is already in git history, so removing the line is not enough.
fix: Rotate the key in the Stripe dashboard first. Then load it from the secrets manager at startup and fail fast if it is missing.

title: JWT decoded without verifying its signature
message: jwt.decode() returns claims without checking the signature or issuer.
why: Any client can forge a token with arbitrary sub and scopes and it will be accepted. Introduced by "auth: accept tokens from legacy issuer".
fix: Verify the token with the issuer public key and pin the algorithm and audience.

title: Campaign HTML rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML without sanitizing
message: campaign.bodyHtml is editable by marketing users in the CMS.
why: A CMS user (or anyone who compromises one) can inject script that runs on the checkout page with access to card-entry iframes and session cookies.
fix: Sanitize with an allow-list before rendering, or render the campaign as structured content.

title: yaml.load with the full Loader allows arbitrary object construction
message: Model configs are pulled from a shared S3 bucket writable by 3 teams.
why: A crafted YAML file can execute code in the scoring service, which has read access to transaction history.
fix: Use safe_load, which only builds plain Python types.

title: unwrap() on a fallible lookup in the posting path can panic the worker
message: Both lookups can fail for postings replayed from the dead-letter queue.
why: A panic aborts the Tokio worker and drops every in-flight posting on it. The function already returns Result, so the error can be propagated.
fix: Map the missing account and conversion failure into LedgerError and use ?.

title: Promise from refreshToken() is neither awaited nor handled
message: A rejected refresh becomes an unhandled rejection and the client keeps the stale token.
why: Callers retry with an expired token and see a burst of 401s; in Node this also crashes the process under --unhandled-rejections=strict.
fix: Await the call, or attach a handler that emits an error event.

title: Error returned by json.Encoder.Encode is ignored
message: Encode can fail on a closed connection or an unsupported value.
why: Silent failures here leave clients with truncated JSON and no server-side log line to correlate.
fix: Check the error and log it with the request ID.

title: Tender validation duplicated across 4 handlers
message: 14 identical lines also in refund.go, capture.go and void.go.
why: The split-tender change already had to fix the same rounding bug in two of the four copies.
fix: Move validation into tender.Validate and call it from each handler.

title: Broad except Exception hides scoring failures and returns 0.0
why: Any feature or model error silently approves the transaction, which is the worst possible fallback for a fraud check.
fix: Catch only expected errors and fail closed.

title: Cognitive complexity of calculate() is 31 (max 15)
why: Tax rules change quarterly; every change here has needed a hotfix in the past year.
fix: Extract a TaxStrategy per region and test each in isolation.

title: unsafe block without a // SAFETY: comment
message: transmute relies on Fixed being #[repr(C)] — not asserted.
why: Tuple layout is unspecified in Rust; a compiler upgrade can silently corrupt every amount built this way.
fix: Construct the struct directly — no unsafe needed.
